content.text:
The original file was empty, so there was no drawing to improve. I rewrote it as a proper SVG scaffold, but could not run a parser against it because the session denied both validation commands.

**What the file was.** A single self-closed root element, 41 bytes, with no width, height, viewBox, or children. Browsers render that as a blank 300 by 150 box, and nothing inside it could ever scale.

**What it is now.** The new file at `/private/tmp/gndfv/0.svg`:

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="100" height="100" viewBox="0 0 100 100" role="img" aria-labelledby="svg-title">
  <title id="svg-title">Untitled</title>
</svg>
```

- **Scales correctly.** The viewBox gives it a coordinate system, and the width and height give it an intrinsic size when placed in an img tag.
- **Accessible.** The image role plus a linked title give screen readers a name instead of silence.
- **Extensible.** The root is now an open element with a child, so shapes can be added directly.

**What was blocked.** Running xmllint to confirm well-formedness and Quick Look to confirm it renders were both auto-denied, since nothing in this session can approve a prompt. I checked the markup by inspection instead. It is three tags with matching closes and quoted attributes, so I am confident it parses, but it has not been machine-verified.

**Assumptions I made.** I chose a square 100 by 100 space and the placeholder title "Untitled" because nothing in the directory indicated the intended size or subject. If you tell me what this SVG should show, or the size it needs to be, I can draw the content or adjust the viewBox.
